probes.support_reason: Deterministic tie-break, all-yes. (1) `File::open("data.txt")?` opens the named file for reading with the standard library only, and it can fail - the `?` is there because it returns `io::Result<File>`. (2) `io::read_to_string(&file)?` reads the entire contents into the text-string local `text` (a `String`, Rust's owned UTF-8 text type). (3) the handle is released when the enclosing scope ends on EVERY exit path: `file` is an owning local, so Reference 'Destructors' drops it at the closing brace, and the `?` on the read line returns THROUGH that drop, so the descriptor is closed exactly once whether the read succeeds or fails. (4) it returns `text.len()`, documented as the length in BYTES, and propagates the failure the way Rust's mechanism requires, by returning `Err` from `read_all`. Verified on the host: with data.txt present the program prints 6 (the file is 'hello\n'); F-2/F-3/F-4 hold under the frozen recipe with no extra flag and no crate. F-6: no normative prohibition or deprecation applies. probes.support_reason: Deterministic tie-break, all-yes. (1) `std::thread::spawn` starts TWO independent units of concurrent execution - real OS threads from the standard library as shipped with rustc 1.95.0, not a cooperative runtime - the first computing 20 and the second 22. (2) `join()` on each handle waits for both to finish. (3) `sum` is bound to the sum of their two results and is produced; the program prints 42. The measured region is written under R1a and contains the launch, the join and the combination; Rust needs NO async runtime entry construct, because `std::thread` is part of the standard library and `main` is an ordinary function - that is a measured property of the language, and the plain non-async `main` wrapper is excluded from the region exactly as the canonical task directs. F-2/F-3/F-4 hold under the frozen recipe with no crate and no extra flag; P-e does not apply (no extra compilation unit and no runtime block). F-6: no normative prohibition or deprecation applies to `thread::spawn` or `JoinHandle::join`. R10 evidence: (a) THE MEASURED FORM, with the two launches written as fully-qualified `std::thread::spawn` paths = 49 tokens, prints 42; (b) the same fragment with `use std::thread;` inside the markers and `thread::spawn` twice = 50 tokens, builds and prints 42 - one token more, so R10 selects (a). Recorded because the choice is not free in the other metrics: the fully-qualified form is also the form that cannot be shadowed, and it is what gives this probe B = 1 below. AUDIT NOTE (F19.P1 measured fragment boundary): canonical-task sub-requirement (3) is 'binds a local `sum` ... and produces it'. Five languages put the production inside the markers (cpp, java, typescript, go, kotlin) and four put it outside (python's `print(sum)`, RUST's `println!`, swift's `print(sum)`, zig's `return sum`). Rule 1.1.3 requires the fragment to denote the same semantic event in all ten and forbids widening one language's fragment or narrowing another's, so the column must pick one boundary. The audit's recommended resolution -- exclude the production statement everywhere, since it is the probe's I/O tail and not the concurrency construct -- is the boundary Rust's frozen fragment ALREADY uses, so no change is made here; the cell is recorded so that the five languages that must move are not moved against an undocumented Rust baseline. If the opposite resolution is adopted, python/rust/swift/zig must take the production in and be re-annotated. The pre-audit ledger reached 30 rows over 13 fact-bearing sites (2.31 per site) against python's 4.76 and cpp's 3.85 on the same probe, and the largest single omission was structural: the SECOND unit's sites -- `let second`, its `spawn` call, its closure, its `join` and its `unwrap` -- carried no rows at all, although A3.4 makes them different entities from the first unit's. Every name in the measured region is a primitive or an attribute fixed by the Reference; nothing is imported, nothing is a method call, and the two operands are the function's own parameters, declared in the same region. AUDIT CORRECTION: the pre-audit B = 1 rested on the assertion that 'every name in the measured region is a primitive or an attribute fixed by the Reference'. `i32` is NOT fixed by the Reference in that sense: it is a PRELUDE NAME, not a keyword (Rust Reference (rustc 1.95.0), https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/ 'Names > Preludes'), and an explicitly declared item shadows it -- which is precisely why `core::primitive` exists.
